node.title: Re: Is there a way to make these two regex lines cleaner?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
You could replace the first line with a [doc://perlop#tr/SEARCHLIST/REPLACEMENTLIST/cdsr|tr///cd], that should be a bit faster. The second line is the usual way to trim whitespace from a string in Perl so it's fine the way it is.

However, "ï»¿" is the [wp://Byte order mark] when the file is encoded in UTF-8 but was opened with the incorrect encoding. So instead of that first regex, you probably want to open the file with open my $fh, '<:raw:encoding(UTF-8)', $filename or die "$filename: $!";, and then do a $line =~ s/\A\N{U+FEFF}//; on the first line of the file. This has the major advantage that any other UTF-8 encoded characters in the file will be decoded correctly - meaning you won't get "strange characters", you'll get the correct Unicode characters, assuming no other encoding issues - and this really is the correct way to solve this issue. If you then still want to turn the text into ASCII-only, see e.g. [mod://Text::Unidecode].

Updated: A few edits for clarification. Also: If you have further issues with encoding, I have some brief advice on what to post to get the best answers [id://1233709|here].
